**DS066** is a medical diagnosis code representing traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage. Within the Danish healthcare system, it plays a specific and critical role in monitoring the safety of anticoagulant treatments for patients with [[atrieflimren]]. 

Because patients with atrial fibrillation are often prescribed blood thinners to prevent strokes, they carry an elevated risk of severe bleeding complications. To measure and improve the quality of care, the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK) tracks the incidence of [[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]] as a key clinical safety indicator [^src1]. DS066 is one of the specific ICD-10 codes used to identify these intracranial bleeding events in the national patient registry, alongside related codes such as [[di60|DI60]], [[di61|DI61]], [[di62|DI62]], [[ds064|DS064]], and [[ds065|DS065]] [^src1]. 

Furthermore, DS066 is included in a broader composite indicator that measures the incidence of any severe bleeding among atrial fibrillation patients [^src1]. This broader metric captures a wide spectrum of hemorrhagic events, combining the intracranial codes (DI60–DS066) with specific codes for gastrointestinal bleeding (e.g., [[dk25-0|DK25.0]]–[[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]]) and urinary or respiratory bleeding (e.g., [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], [[dr31|DR31]]) [^src1]. By capturing DS066 and related codes in these registries, health authorities can evaluate the real-world safety profiles of different anticoagulant therapies and adjust clinical guidelines accordingly.
